jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Office for National Statistics (ONS) is the UK’s largest producer of official statistics, covering a range of key economic, social and demographic topics. These include measuring changes in the value of the UK economy, estimating the size, geographic distribution, and characteristics of the population, and providing indicators of price inflation, employment, earnings, crime, and migration.

We are transforming how we use data to better understand and measure the UK’s economy and society, to drive better decision making, and to improve the lives of citizens. A core part of this work is the development of our Geospatial Strategy and capability - driving the effective use of geospatial methods across the organisation to add maximum value to ONS statistics.

In July 2025, HM Government commissioned ONS to conduct a mandatory, questionnaire-based, whole-population census of England and Wales in 2031. We have started to prepare for Census 2031, with a Census Taskforce scoping plans and building on the experience of Census 2021. We are preparing for an inclusive, digital-first census, working with devolved governments to support coherent UK outputs and maximising the benefits from our work with administrative data to date. ONS’ Data Products, Services and Governance (DPSG) Directorate provides many of the data products and services that are a vital part of the infrastructure of Census and wider ONS. Team specialisms include data architecture, various engineering functions, acquisition and governance, and data linkage. DPSG also includes a small but dynamic team of geospatial specialists, providing essential geospatial data products, infrastructure, expertise and guidance to ONS business areas and across wider government.

We’re looking for an enthusiastic and talented Geospatial Analyst, to help us drive forward our ambitions, bring creativity and new ways of thinking. We want to build teams with a range of skills, where the team-members’ strengths complement each other. If you have strong technical skills and interpersonal skills, and you are interested in using your geospatial analytical skills to help transform the way we use data across government, then we are interested in your application.

Job Description

A Geospatial Analyst applies expertise in geography and spatial/location data to deliver high‑quality analysis and geographical products across the office. They lead and support research and analytical projects where location data is central, while actively exploring innovative technologies to improve efficiency and enhance outputs in line with evolving organisational needs.

As the successful candidate, you will work on a broad range of geospatial projects—from creating new geographies to processing spatial/location datasets to generate insights and indicators. You will help advance geospatial analytical methods, introducing new approaches to data processing and interpretation.

You will collaborate closely with colleagues and receive guidance from senior team members, contributing to a supportive and knowledge‑sharing environment. Continuous professional development is encouraged, and you will be expected to stay up‑to‑date with emerging geospatial technologies, datasets, and analytical techniques.

Key Responsibilities

The Successful Candidate Will Undertake Activities Such As

Work on specific project alone or with support from team members.
Use appropriate tools and techniques and/or approaches to meet stakeholder requirements
Apply a mixture of GIS, coding, analytical and statistical methodologies to produce the necessary outputs
Collect, collate and prepare datasets for analytical inputs.
Review and assess new data sources
Explore and evaluate new datasets, technologies and techniques to maintain and update training packages.
Quality assess and peer review colleagues outputs to ensure a quality service
Work with academic and commercial experts on new methods and analysis tasks to improve existing or create new outputs
Support in the production of training/teaching material for internal and external stakeholders
Engage in activities to support the geography community across ONS and Government (e.g. GGP)

Person specification

Essential Skill Criteria

Candidates should demonstrate experience for the following skills at the Working Level
– Applies knowledge and experience of the skill, including tools and techniques, adopting those most appropriate for the environment.

(GGP) Geographic knowledge

The understanding of geographic processes and how they shape the physical and human world at different scales, and its application i.e. the analysis, storage, visualisation, and management of geographic data

(GGP) Geospatial analysis & problem solving

The use of appropriate techniques to analyse spatial and non-spatial data in order to solve data problems, including based on spatial relationships. Able to manipulate, integrate and aggregate data based on its spatial reference.

(GGP) Geographic compliance

Understand and comply with relevant national and international geospatial frameworks and best practice (e.g. statutory requirements, standards, etc.) impacting and related to the specific discipline. Legal and ethical issues related to geospatial data including rights, liability, privacy and access.

(GGP) Quality Assurance and Control

The ability to review and assessment of own and others’ quality of work through the maintenance of a desired level of quality in outputs and ensuring precision and accuracy of datasets and methods used

(DDAT) Data preparation and linkage

The ability to conduct data preparation and linkage which involved cleansing, modelling, transforming and assuring the quality of data so that it is usable and reproducible, as well as aiding the creation of a more informative product.

Qualifications

At least either an undergraduate degree, or equivalent qualification, with relevance to the job description OR at least 1 years’ experience in a role/study relevant to the job description.

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

Changing and Improving
Working Together
Communicating and Influencing
Delivering at Pace

Technical skills

We'll assess you against these technical skills during the selection process:

(GGP) Geospatial Software and Systems - The use of desktop and online tools for managing, analysing and displaying geospatial data, interactively or in workflows
(GGP) Geospatial Coding - Use of coding libraries in the analysis of geospatial data or the automation of geospatial processes and application of relevant optimisation techniques.

Description

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring a Permit Writer
(Environmental Specialist 4) within the Water Resources Program. (WR)

Location:

Headquarters Office in Lacey, WA .
Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the duty station.

Schedule

This position is eligible for telework and flexible schedule options.
This position is required to be in the office 2 days each week, on Tuesday and Wednesday.
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Application Timeline

Apply by October 11, 2026
Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

In this role, you will have the exciting opportunity to implement Washington Water Law. You will be responsible for managing, processing, evaluating, and drafting support documents for water right decisions. This includes completing investigations by researching, collecting, and analyzing technical data and other information to support water right decisions. You will have the opportunity to identify issues and find possible solutions. You will get to interact with other government agencies, municipalities, and citizens that are looking for water for their projects or homes. There is also an opportunity to let your GIS and mapping skills shine. We are looking for people that want to make a difference, enjoy being part of a team, and are willing to learn.

What You Will Do

Recommend and process water right decisions.
Conduct investigations and technical reviews to support decisions.
Evaluate projects for feasibility, compliance with laws, regulations, and policies.
Work with other local and state government agencies and Tribes regarding Washington water law.
Respond to inquiries from water right applicants, their consultants, other agency staff and the public.
Develop maps and locate water rights using GIS and web mapping tools and software.

Qualifications

For detailed information on how we calculate experience and responses to other frequently asked questions, please visit our Recruitment website .

Required Qualifications

Nine years
of combined education and/or experience performing related to the duties of the position, that includes the following:

Experience collecting, researching, and analyzing complex hydrologic or hydrogeologic data to support technical evaluations and regulatory decisions.
Ability to apply scientific, hydrologic, or hydrogeologic findings and/or principles to permitting related decisions.
Demonstrated skill in preparing technical written reports that summarize analyses, findings, and defensible recommendations for permitting decisions.
Ability to conduct and interpret field investigations under the oversight of a licensed hydrogeologist, including groundwater and surface water related analyses.
Experience reviewing proposed water related projects for legal, technical, and policy compliance.
Strong communication and customer service skills, with the ability to interact professionally with applicants, consultants, tribal governments, partner agencies, and the public.
Ability to manage and monitor complex permitting systems, for example water right authorizations.
Familiarity with GIS and mapping tools to analyze and document water rights information, and ability to serve as a technical resource on mapping related tasks.
Ability to mentor and support junior staff, collaborate on statewide workgroups, and independently manage workload priorities in a regulatory environment.

Education:
Involving a major study in environmental, physical, or one of the natural sciences; environmental or natural science interdisciplinary studies; environmental planning, or related studies.

Examples Of How To Qualify

9 years of experience.
8 years of experience AND 30-59 semester or 45-89 quarter college credits.
7 years of experience AND 60-89 semester or 90-134 quarter college credits (Associate’s degree).
6 years of experience AND 90-119 semester or 135-179 quarter college credits.
5 years of experience AND a Bachelor’s degree.
3 years of experience AND a Master’s degree.
2 years of experience AND a Ph.D.

Desired Qualifications

Bachelor Degree in environmental, physical, or one of the natural sciences; environmental or natural science interdisciplinary studies; environmental planning, or an academic discipline related to the duties of the position.
Demonstrated professional experience implementing water resource management laws and rules Knowledge of Washington State water law, related rules, policies, and water rights permitting processes,
Experience in applied geology, hydrogeology, or related disciplines.

If you are excited about this role and meet the required qualifications, we encourage you to apply. Desired qualifications reflect additional knowledge, skills, or experience that are nice to have but not required. Studies have shown that some applicants, especially women and people of color, are less likely to apply unless they meet every listed qualification. At the Department of Ecology, we are dedicated to building a diverse and authentic workplace centered in belonging, and we welcome applicants with varied backgrounds and unique perspectives.

Supplemental Information

Ecology does not use the E-Verify system; therefore, we are not eligible to extend STEM Optional Practical Training (OPT). For more information, please visit www.uscis.gov .

Our Commitment to DEIR

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Respect (DEIR)
are core values central to Ecology's work. We strive to be a workplace where we are esteemed for sharing our authentic identities, while advancing our individual professional goals and collaborating to protect, preserve, and enhance the environment for current and future generations.

Diversity:
We celebrate and appreciate diversity; our unique perspectives and abilities enrich us all and lead to innovative approaches and solutions.

Equity:
We champion equity, recognizing that each of us need different things to thrive.

Inclusion:
We intentionally create and hold space so that we all have meaningful opportunities to participate and contribute to Ecology’s work.

Respect:
We treat each other with respect and dignity, acknowledging the inherent worth of our diverse perspectives and lived experiences, even in times of uncertainty and disagreement.

We believe that DEIR is both a goal and an action. We are on a journey, honoring our shared humanity and taking steps to demonstrate our commitment to a vision where each of us is heard, seen, and valued.

Application Process

Ecology seeks diverse applicants: We view diversity, equity, inclusion, and respect through a broad lens including race, ethnicity, class, age, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, immigration status, military background, language, education, life experience, physical disability, neurodiversity, and intersectional identities. Qualified job seekers from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

How To Apply

Click “Apply” at the top of this page. Complete the entire application, including full work history and responses to all supplemental questions, and attach:

Cover letter, describing your interest in and qualifications for this position
Resume

Because we base our selection on the information you provide, it is in your best interest to complete the application thoroughly. A resume will not substitute for the “work experience” section of the application or vice versa. Applications with blank fields or supplemental question responses with comments such as “see resume” may be considered incomplete.

For detailed application information, please visit our Recruitment website.

Application Attestation: By submitting an application, you are affirming that the information contained in your application and on all attachments is complete and truthful. jobs.description:
Description

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring a Regional Compliance Inspector - Refrigerant Management Program (Environmental Specialist 3)
within the Climate Pollution Reduction Program (CPRP).

Location:

Northwest Region Office in Shoreline, WA .
The salary listed includes 5% premium pay due to the position location in King County.
Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the duty station.

Schedule

This position is eligible for telework and flexible schedule options.
A minimum of one day per week is required in the office. This position is expected to be in the office for a full workday every Tuesday.
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Application Timeline

Apply by October 4, 2026.
Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

Do you want your work to directly reduce climate-polluting emissions in Washington State? Does the idea of helping businesses understand and comply with environmental regulations appeal to you? Are you interested in conducting on-the-ground inspections and working one-on-one with the regulated community to keep refrigerant systems operating safely and responsibly? If you answered “yes,” then this role may be a great fit for you!

The Refrigerant Management Program (RMP) regulates facilities with large refrigeration and air-conditioning systems to ensure they follow best practices that reduce leaks of climate-polluting fluorinated gases. As a Regional Compliance Inspector, you will help facilities register in the RMP, provide technical guidance, and conduct inspections across the Northwest region to verify compliance.

Your work will directly support Ecology’s statewide effort to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from refrigeration systems. You will develop specialized knowledge of Washington’s hydrofluorocarbon (HFC) regulations, interpret technical requirements for the public, and help facilities identify practical, cost-effective ways to meet their obligations. If you are motivated by fieldwork, enjoy problem-solving, and want your work to contribute to meaningful climate solutions, this position offers a rewarding opportunity.

In This Role, You Will

Provide technical assistance to facility owners and operators, helping them understand refrigerant rules, reporting obligations, and how to comply with RMP processes.
Explain refrigerant regulations in a clear, accessible way during one-on-one interactions, online office hours, and public meetings.
Assist facility owners and operators with entering required data into the Refrigeration and Air-Conditioning Management Program (RAMP) database.

Conduct inspections of facilities subject to the Refrigerant Management Program (RMP), both remotely and in person.
Verify that facilities are following state and federal HFC rules and maintaining records that meet program requirements.
Review RMP registrations and annual reports, identify potential compliance issues, and help return facilities to compliance through follow-up actions.
If necessary, collect and document information necessary for enforcement actions.

Coordinate with teammates across the state to ensure consistent application of inspection procedures and regulatory interpretations, and on potential ways to improve compliance.
Collaborate with Ecology outreach staff to promote awareness of climate-friendly refrigerants and refrigerant alternatives.
Develop/maintain professional knowledge of applicable HFC laws, refrigerant technologies, leak detection methods, and emerging industry issues.

Qualifications

For detailed information on how we calculate experience and responses to other frequently asked questions, please visit our Recruitment website .

Required Qualifications

Six years of experience and/or education related to the duties of the position, which must include the following:

Regulatory Application and Interpretation – Demonstrated competence with interpreting and applying environmental or regulatory requirements to accurately assess facility compliance and support consistent implementation of program obligations.
Inspection and Field Evaluation – Experienced in conducting structured compliance inspections or field evaluations to determine whether facilities follow required procedures and maintain accurate operational or recordkeeping practices.
Professional Judgment and Compliance Determination – Skilled at using analytical thinking, evidence review, and sound professional judgment to identify potential violations, recommend corrective actions, and support facilities in returning to sustained compliance.
Technical Assistance and Communication – Ability to explain complex regulatory or technical information in clear, understandable terms to help regulated entities meet program requirements and successfully use required database tools.
Collaborative Coordination Across Teams – Demonstrated competence with coordinating work and sharing information across the regional inspection team to ensure consistent approaches to inspections, education, compliance assistance, and enforcement activities.
Data, System, and Technology Proficiency – Skilled with learning and using program-specific databases and analytical tools to track inspection activities, organize documentation, analyze compliance trends, and prepare accurate reports that support program decision-making.
Independent Project and Workload Management – Ability to independently plan, prioritize, and complete inspections, follow-up activities, and documentation to meet program expectations and support timely, effective compliance outcomes.

Job Summary

The Office for National Statistics (ONS) is the UK’s largest producer of official statistics, covering a range of key economic, social and demographic topics. These include measuring changes in the value of the UK economy, estimating the size, geographic distribution, and characteristics of the population, and providing indicators of price inflation, employment, earnings, crime, and migration.

We are transforming how we use data to better understand and measure the UK’s economy and society, to drive better decision making, and to improve the lives of citizens. A core part of this work is the development of our Geospatial Strategy and capability - driving the effective use of geospatial methods across the organisation to add maximum value to ONS statistics.

In July 2025, HM Government commissioned ONS to conduct a mandatory, questionnaire-based, whole-population census of England and Wales in 2031. We have started to prepare for Census 2031, with a Census Taskforce scoping plans and building on the experience of Census 2021. We are preparing for an inclusive, digital-first census, working with devolved governments to support coherent UK outputs and maximising the benefits from our work with administrative data to date. ONS’ Data Products, Services and Governance (DPSG) Directorate provides many of the data products and services that are a vital part of the infrastructure of Census and wider ONS. Team specialisms include data architecture, various engineering functions, acquisition and governance, and data linkage. DPSG also includes a small but dynamic team of geospatial specialists, providing essential geospatial data products, infrastructure, expertise and guidance to ONS business areas and across wider government.

We’re looking for an enthusiastic and talented Geospatial Analyst, to help us drive forward our ambitions, bring creativity and new ways of thinking. We want to build teams with a range of skills, where the team-members’ strengths complement each other. If you have strong technical skills and interpersonal skills, and you are interested in using your geospatial analytical skills to help transform the way we use data across government, then we are interested in your application.

Job Description

A Geospatial Analyst applies expertise in geography and spatial/location data to deliver high‑quality analysis and geographical products across the office. They lead and support research and analytical projects where location data is central, while actively exploring innovative technologies to improve efficiency and enhance outputs in line with evolving organisational needs.

As the successful candidate, you will work on a broad range of geospatial projects—from creating new geographies to processing spatial/location datasets to generate insights and indicators. You will help advance geospatial analytical methods, introducing new approaches to data processing and interpretation.

You will collaborate closely with colleagues and receive guidance from senior team members, contributing to a supportive and knowledge‑sharing environment. Continuous professional development is encouraged, and you will be expected to stay up‑to‑date with emerging geospatial technologies, datasets, and analytical techniques.

Key Responsibilities

The Successful Candidate Will Undertake Activities Such As

Work on specific project alone or with support from team members.
Use appropriate tools and techniques and/or approaches to meet stakeholder requirements
Apply a mixture of GIS, coding, analytical and statistical methodologies to produce the necessary outputs
Collect, collate and prepare datasets for analytical inputs.
Review and assess new data sources
Explore and evaluate new datasets, technologies and techniques to maintain and update training packages.
Quality assess and peer review colleagues outputs to ensure a quality service
Work with academic and commercial experts on new methods and analysis tasks to improve existing or create new outputs
Support in the production of training/teaching material for internal and external stakeholders
Engage in activities to support the geography community across ONS and Government (e.g. GGP)

Person specification

Essential Skill Criteria

Candidates should demonstrate experience for the following skills at the Working Level
– Applies knowledge and experience of the skill, including tools and techniques, adopting those most appropriate for the environment.

(GGP) Geographic knowledge

The understanding of geographic processes and how they shape the physical and human world at different scales, and its application i.e. the analysis, storage, visualisation, and management of geographic data

(GGP) Geospatial analysis & problem solving

The use of appropriate techniques to analyse spatial and non-spatial data in order to solve data problems, including based on spatial relationships. Able to manipulate, integrate and aggregate data based on its spatial reference.

(GGP) Geographic compliance

Understand and comply with relevant national and international geospatial frameworks and best practice (e.g. statutory requirements, standards, etc.) impacting and related to the specific discipline. (GGP) Quality Assurance and Control

The ability to review and assessment of own and others’ quality of work through the maintenance of a desired level of quality in outputs and ensuring precision and accuracy of datasets and methods used

(DDAT) Data preparation and linkage

The ability to conduct data preparation and linkage which involved cleansing, modelling, transforming and assuring the quality of data so that it is usable and reproducible, as well as aiding the creation of a more informative product.

At least either an undergraduate degree, or equivalent qualification, with relevance to the job description OR at least 1 years’ experience in a role/study relevant to the job description.

Working Together

Delivering at Pace

(GGP) Geospatial Software and Systems - The use of desktop and online tools for managing, analysing and displaying geospatial data, interactively or in workflows

There is also an opportunity to let your GIS and mapping skills shine. We are looking for people that want to make a difference, enjoy being part of a team, and are willing to learn.

Recommend and process water right decisions.
Conduct investigations and technical reviews to support decisions.
Evaluate projects for feasibility, compliance with laws, regulations, and policies.
Work with other local and state government agencies and Tribes regarding Washington water law.
Respond to inquiries from water right applicants, their consultants, other agency staff and the public.
Develop maps and locate water rights using GIS and web mapping tools and software.

of combined education and/or experience performing related to the duties of the position, that includes the following:

Experience collecting, researching, and analyzing complex hydrologic or hydrogeologic data to support technical evaluations and regulatory decisions.

Vi tilbyder dig En spændende stilling med stor variation i opgaverne og høj grad af selvstændighed. Du bliver en del af et stærkt fagligt miljø, hvor samarbejde, videndeling og udvikling er en naturlig del af hverdagen. Samtidig får du mulighed for at arbejde med konkrete problemstillinger, hvor dine analyser og løsninger hurtigt omsættes til praksis. Du får en unik mulighed for at arbejde på tværs af to fagområder og bidrage til både udviklingen af kommunens natur- og klimaprojekter samt den daglige drift af veje og grønne områder. Har forståelse for samspillet mellem data, drift og beslutningsprocesser. Kan arbejde struktureret med komplekse datamængder. Har en relevant uddannelse som eksempelvis teknisk designer eller anden tilsvarende. Gerne har erfaring fra kommunal, offentlig eller teknisk virksomhed, men det er ikke et krav. Vi forventer, at du personligt Arbejder selvstændigt og tager ansvar for dine opgaver. Er nysgerrig og opsøgende i forhold til nye opgaver og problemstillinger. Kan samarbejde på tværs af faggrupper og afdelinger. Er serviceminded og har fokus på at skabe værdi for dem, du samarbejder med. Har gode kommunikationsevner og kan formidle tekniske problemstillinger på en forståelig måde. Ansættelsesvilkår Løn- og ansættelsesvilkår efter gældende overenskomst og principperne i Ny Løn. Vi lægger vægt på faglig kvalitet, samarbejde og en uformel omgangtone. Samtidig arbejder vi målrettet med digitalisering og anvendelse af data som grundlag for bedre beslutninger og smartere arbejdsgange. Lyst til at høre mere? About The West Region Delivery Team

The West Region Delivery Team consortium comprises Abergeldie Complex Infrastructure and Fulton Hogan for construction, Programmed for maintenance and facility management, and Stantec and Atlas for design and engineering.

The West Region Delivery Team is integrated with Sydney Water under a collaborative contracting framework, Partnering for Success (P4S). The West Region Delivery Team has been engaged to deliver design, construction, maintenance and facility management services for a ten (10) year program across Sydney Water's wastewater, water and recycled water systems.

About The Opportunity

We are seeking an Environmental Advisor to join the West Region Delivery Team, supporting the delivery of a diverse portfolio of water and wastewater infrastructure projects for Sydney Water.

Supporting multiple construction projects across the program, you will provide environmental advice, identify and manage risks, implement controls and help ensure compliance throughout project delivery. Working closely with operational and project teams, you will help drive environmental performance and best practice across active construction sites.

Key Responsibilities Include

Providing day-to-day environmental support and guidance to project delivery teams.
Conducting environmental inspections, audits and compliance assessments across construction sites.
Monitoring and reporting on compliance with environmental management plans, approvals, permits and legislative requirements.
Supporting the implementation and maintenance of erosion and sediment controls
Assisting with environmental risk assessments and identifying opportunities to improve environmental performance.
Investigating environmental incidents, non-conformances and complaints, and supporting corrective actions.
Preparing environmental reports, monitoring records and project compliance documentation.
Delivering environmental awareness training and guidance to project personnel and subcontractors.
Liaising with clients, regulators and key stakeholders on environmental matters.
Supporting the development and continuous improvement of environmental management processes and systems.

What You'll Bring To The Team

Description

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring a Regional Compliance Inspector - Refrigerant Management Program (Environmental Specialist 3)
within the Climate Pollution Reduction Program (CPRP).

Location:

Northwest Region Office in Shoreline, WA .
The salary listed includes 5% premium pay due to the position location in King County.
Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the duty station.

Schedule

This position is eligible for telework and flexible schedule options.
A minimum of one day per week is required in the office. This position is expected to be in the office for a full workday every Tuesday.
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Application Timeline

Apply by October 4, 2026.
Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

Do you want your work to directly reduce climate-polluting emissions in Washington State? Does the idea of helping businesses understand and comply with environmental regulations appeal to you? Are you interested in conducting on-the-ground inspections and working one-on-one with the regulated community to keep refrigerant systems operating safely and responsibly? If you answered “yes,” then this role may be a great fit for you!

The Refrigerant Management Program (RMP) regulates facilities with large refrigeration and air-conditioning systems to ensure they follow best practices that reduce leaks of climate-polluting fluorinated gases. As a Regional Compliance Inspector, you will help facilities register in the RMP, provide technical guidance, and conduct inspections across the Northwest region to verify compliance.

Your work will directly support Ecology’s statewide effort to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from refrigeration systems. You will develop specialized knowledge of Washington’s hydrofluorocarbon (HFC) regulations, interpret technical requirements for the public, and help facilities identify practical, cost-effective ways to meet their obligations. If you are motivated by fieldwork, enjoy problem-solving, and want your work to contribute to meaningful climate solutions, this position offers a rewarding opportunity.

In This Role, You Will

Provide technical assistance to facility owners and operators, helping them understand refrigerant rules, reporting obligations, and how to comply with RMP processes.
Explain refrigerant regulations in a clear, accessible way during one-on-one interactions, online office hours, and public meetings.
Assist facility owners and operators with entering required data into the Refrigeration and Air-Conditioning Management Program (RAMP) database.

Conduct inspections of facilities subject to the Refrigerant Management Program (RMP), both remotely and in person.
Verify that facilities are following state and federal HFC rules and maintaining records that meet program requirements.
Review RMP registrations and annual reports, identify potential compliance issues, and help return facilities to compliance through follow-up actions.
If necessary, collect and document information necessary for enforcement actions.

Coordinate with teammates across the state to ensure consistent application of inspection procedures and regulatory interpretations, and on potential ways to improve compliance.
Collaborate with Ecology outreach staff to promote awareness of climate-friendly refrigerants and refrigerant alternatives.
Develop/maintain professional knowledge of applicable HFC laws, refrigerant technologies, leak detection methods, and emerging industry issues.

Qualifications

For detailed information on how we calculate experience and responses to other frequently asked questions, please visit our Recruitment website .

Required Qualifications

Six years of experience and/or education related to the duties of the position, which must include the following:

Regulatory Application and Interpretation – Demonstrated competence with interpreting and applying environmental or regulatory requirements to accurately assess facility compliance and support consistent implementation of program obligations.
Inspection and Field Evaluation – Experienced in conducting structured compliance inspections or field evaluations to determine whether facilities follow required procedures and maintain accurate operational or recordkeeping practices.
Professional Judgment and Compliance Determination – Skilled at using analytical thinking, evidence review, and sound professional judgment to identify potential violations, recommend corrective actions, and support facilities in returning to sustained compliance.
Technical Assistance and Communication – Ability to explain complex regulatory or technical information in clear, understandable terms to help regulated entities meet program requirements and successfully use required database tools.
Collaborative Coordination Across Teams – Demonstrated competence with coordinating work and sharing information across the regional inspection team to ensure consistent approaches to inspections, education, compliance assistance, and enforcement activities.
Data, System, and Technology Proficiency – Skilled with learning and using program-specific databases and analytical tools to track inspection activities, organize documentation, analyze compliance trends, and prepare accurate reports that support program decision-making.
Independent Project and Workload Management – Ability to independently plan, prioritize, and complete inspections, follow-up activities, and documentation to meet program expectations and support timely, effective compliance outcomes.
Research and Emerging Issues Analysis – Experienced in gaining understanding of new or evolving technical, regulatory, or environmental issues to identify trends, evaluate potential impacts on program implementation, and recommend improvements that strengthen compliance and reduce emissions.

Education
involving a major study in environmental, physical, or one of the natural sciences; Environmental Health or Occupational Safety and Health (OSHA) studies; environmental planning, or an academic discipline related to the duties of the position.

Examples Of How To Qualify

6 years of experience.
5 years of experience AND 30-59 semester or 45-89 quarter college credits.
4 years of experience AND 60-89 semester or 90-134 quarter college credits (Associate’s degree).
3 years of experience AND 90-119 semester or 135-179 quarter college credits.
2 years of experience AND a Bachelor’s degree.
A Master’s degree or above.

Special Requirements/Conditions Of Employment

Must possess and maintain a valid state driver’s license or provide alternate reliable transportation for travel throughout Ecology’s Northwest Region area.

Desired Qualifications

Environmental Compliance and Inspection Experience – Experienced in performing environmental compliance, inspection, or auditing work to assess facility operations, evaluate records or procedures, and recommend corrective actions that strengthen adherence to regulatory requirements.
Climate and Air Quality Knowledge – Demonstrated competence with understanding air quality concepts and climate change science to evaluate how refrigerant emissions and compliance activities support statewide emission reduction goals.
Greenhouse Gas Program Familiarity – Experienced in working with state or federal greenhouse gas reduction programs to understand how HFC-related requirements fit within broader regulatory or climate-policy frameworks.
Program-Specific Technical Learning – Ability to quickly learn and apply new technical subject matter, including refrigerant types, climate-friendly alternatives, and leak detection methods, to support high-quality inspections and compliance assistance.

If you are excited about this role and meet the required qualifications, we encourage you to apply. Desired qualifications reflect additional knowledge, skills, or experience that are nice to have but not required . Studies have shown that some applicants, especially women and people of color, are less likely to apply unless they meet every listed qualification. At the Department of Ecology, we are dedicated to building a diverse and authentic workplace centered in belonging, and we welcome applicants with varied backgrounds and unique perspectives.

Supplemental Information

Ecology does not use the E-Verify system; therefore, we are not eligible to extend STEM Optional Practical Training (OPT). For more information, please visit www.uscis.gov .

Our Commitment to DEIR

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Respect (DEIR)
are core values central to Ecology's work. We strive to be a workplace where we are esteemed for sharing our authentic identities, while advancing our individual professional goals and collaborating to protect, preserve, and enhance the environment for current and future generations.

Diversity:
We celebrate and appreciate diversity; our unique perspectives and abilities enrich us all and lead to innovative approaches and solutions.

Equity:
We champion equity, recognizing that each of us need different things to thrive.

Inclusion:
We intentionally create and hold space so that we all have meaningful opportunities to participate and contribute to Ecology’s work.

Respect:
We treat each other with respect and dignity, acknowledging the inherent worth of our diverse perspectives and lived experiences, even in times of uncertainty and disagreement.

We believe that DEIR is both a goal and an action. We are on a journey, honoring our shared humanity and taking steps to demonstrate our commitment to a vision where each of us is heard, seen, and valued.

Application Process

Ecology seeks diverse applicants: We view diversity, equity, inclusion, and respect through a broad lens including race, ethnicity, class, age, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, immigration status, military background, language, education, life experience, physical disability, neurodiversity, and intersectional identities. Qualified job seekers from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

How To Apply

Click “Apply” at the top of this page. Complete the entire application, including full work history and responses to all supplemental questions, and attach:

Cover letter, describing your interest in and qualifications for this position
Resume

A resume will not substitute for the “work experience” section of the application or vice versa. Applications with blank fields or supplemental question responses with comments such as “see resume” may be considered incomplete.

For detailed application information, please visit our Recruitment website.

The state may verify this information, and any false or misleading answers may result in rejection of your application or dismissal if employed.
